history.period: Gupta period, 5th-6th century CE (some sources give 5th-7th century - verify)
history.summary: MULTI-RELIGIOUS ARCHAEOLOGICAL SITE, not an active temple: five small rock-cut shrines carved directly from granite boulders on a small hill overlooking the Ganges, with intricate carvings of Hindu, Buddhist and Jain deities (forms of Shiva, Vishnu and Surya). One of the earliest known rock-cut architectural ensembles of the Gupta period - the 'Golden Age' craftsmanship is noted for exceptional detail. Visited by the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang in the 7th century CE. Protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). CSV town 'Bhagalpur' is approximate - the site is at Kahalgaon (Colgong), about 8 km west of Bhagalpur city. COORDINATES APPROXIMATE: no geocoder POI exists for the rock-cut site itself; coordinates used are for the Kahalgaon area and should be verified on the ground.

name: Colganj Rock Cut Temple
town: Colganj (Kahalgaon) - CSV town 'Bhagalpur' is approximate; the site is at Kahalgaon (Colgong), about 8 km west of Bhagalpur city
town_description: Kahalgaon (historically Colgong or Colganj) is a town and subdivision of Bhagalpur district on the banks of the Ganges, about 25 km east of Bhagalpur city. It is said to be named after the sage Kahol, was visited by Xuanzang in the 7th century, and later hosted the Vikramshila Mahavihara founded by King Dharmapala in the 8th century; in modern times it is known for the NTPC thermal power plant set up in 1985.
tradition: Multi-religious (Hindu, Jain and Buddhist carvings; primarily Shaivite)

travel.road: NH-80 via Kahalgaon; the site is on the southern banks of the Ganges near Kahalgaon.
